Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent

Class ConnectionResolver

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.ConnectionResolver
public final class ConnectionResolver extends Object
Maps connection names to query factories, so a model reaches the database named by its connectionName().

Pass a resolver to ModelQuery.using(ConnectionResolver), or bind a model to one factory with ModelQuery.on(QueryFactory). For the Laravel-like path where new User().save() just works, install a process-wide default with setDefault(ConnectionResolver). Registration and lookup are safe across threads.

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static ConnectionResolver of(DatabaseManager manager)
      Creates a resolver that reads its connections from a database manager.

      A name is resolved with DatabaseManager.query(String), so a connection is built the first time a model uses it; null takes the manager's default connection. The resolver owns no state: register(String, QueryFactory) and setDefaultConnection(String) throw UnsupportedOperationException; change the manager instead.

      Parameters:
      manager - the database manager, never null
      Returns:
      the manager-backed resolver, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if manager is null

    • register

      Returns:

    • setDefault

      public static ConnectionResolver.Installation setDefault(ConnectionResolver resolver)
      Installs a resolver as the process-wide default for models not bound to a factory or resolver. Closing the returned handle puts back the resolver that was the default before, if this one is still installed.
      Parameters:
      resolver - the resolver, never null
      Returns:
      the handle that uninstalls it, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if resolver is null
      API Note:
      Process-wide state: every thread and every model class sees it. Prefer ModelQuery.on(QueryFactory) or ModelQuery.using(ConnectionResolver); in tests, install with try-with-resources or call resetDefault() afterwards.
